curriculum.lesson_evidence: Cause-and-effect reading finds what makes something happen and what results from it in an explanation text.
curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point.

lesson.child_mission: Cause-and-effect reading finds what makes something happen and what results from it in an explanation text.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same strategy to an unfamiliar topic or audience, then compare the effect of two different choices.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Mark cause and effect: "The soil dried out, so the seedlings wilted."

FEEDBACK
Cause: soil dried out. Effect: seedlings wilted.

CHECK
Two events next to each other are not always cause and effect.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Read two short explanation paragraphs. For each, list two cause–effect pairs and one sentence that only describes without causing. Quote the signal words you used.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Cause-and-effect reading finds what makes something happen and what results from it in an explanation text.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Read two short explanation paragraphs. For each, list two cause–effect pairs and one sentence that only describes without causing. Quote the signal words you used. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Cause: soil dried out. Effect: seedlings wilted. Reasoning: I used cause by attending to effect and explain why it matters rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Two events next to each other are not always cause and effect. Correction: Cause: soil dried out. Effect: seedlings wilted. Why: the correction restores accurate use of cause.

Parent: Likely misconception: Two events next to each other are not always cause and effect. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating cause on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with cause, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Require independently produced work with a specific supporting detail. / Require misconception + correction + purpose-linked reason..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
"Because the sun heats the puddle, the water evaporates." Cause: sun heats. Effect: water evaporates.

TRY FIRST
Mark cause and effect: "The soil dried out, so the seedlings wilted."

FEEDBACK
Cause: soil dried out. Effect: seedlings wilted.
teach_steps.explain:
Cause-and-effect reading finds what makes something happen and what results from it in an explanation text.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
teach_steps.notice: Two events next to each other are not always cause and effect. Correct the meaning, not just the appearance.
